verdict.rationale: Highnote documents its own webhook notifications. Developers can pick which events go to each webhook, payloads are signed with a rotatable key, and events can be replayed from a log. Refunds are also available via API. However, nothing shows that clearings, refunds, reversals, or chargebacks are emitted as webhook event types, and chargebacks appear to be handled by an in-house disputes team. Missing for 10: documented clearing/settlement webhook events, refund/reversal/chargeback event types, stable transaction identifiers linking auth to post-auth events, an event catalog or payload schema, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, post-auth events are as programmatic as auth — clearings, refunds, reversals, and chargebacks arrive as webhooks with stable transaction identifiers, so my own ledger never drifts

citations.quote: You can configure specific events to be delivered to each webhook
Highnote supports notifications that let you monitor and respond to events in your Highnote integration.
The signing key used to verify payloads is modifiable using the `rotateNotificationTargetSigningKey` mutation.
You can use this log to monitor events, view event details, and replay events.
Authorize funds before an agent commits, capture only what is needed, and refund programmatically. The full payment lifecycle is available via API.
